options: A discrete category label
A continuous numeric value, by fitting a straight line (or hyperplane) to the data
A probability distribution over classes only
A cluster assignment
questions.explain: Linear regression fits a straight line (or hyperplane with multiple features) to model the relationship between features and a continuous numeric output.

questions.q: In the equation y_pred = weight * x + bias, what does training actually find?
options: The training dataset itself
The values of weight and bias that best fit the data
A new feature to add to the dataset
The number of epochs to run
questions.explain: A simple linear regression's entire learned model is just its weight and bias; training searches for the values of those two numbers that fit the data best.

questions.q: What does "best fit" mean for a linear regression line?
options: The line that passes through the most individual data points exactly
The line that minimizes the total squared distance between each point and the line's prediction
The line with the steepest possible slope
The line chosen at random from several candidates
questions.explain: Ordinary least squares defines "best fit" as the line minimizing total squared error — squaring makes all errors positive and penalizes large misses more heavily.

questions.q: In the lesson's scikit-learn example, why does the same line fit on the training set still track the trend in the separate test set?
options: Because the test set was used to fit the line too
Because the line memorized the exact test points
Because it captured a real, generalizable pattern rather than quirks specific to the training points
Because test sets always match training sets exactly
questions.explain: The line was fit only on the training data, yet still tracks the trend in unseen test data — exactly the behavior you want from a model that has learned the real underlying pattern rather than memorizing specifics.

questions.q: What is the core limitation of linear regression?
options: It cannot be trained quickly
It requires labeled data to train, unlike other models
It can only represent relationships that are actually linear, and will underfit a genuinely curved relationship
It can only be used with exactly one feature
questions.explain: Because the model is fundamentally a straight line (or flat hyperplane), it cannot capture a curved relationship no matter how much data it's given — that's a modeling limitation, not a training problem.
